none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

results.references: - Sayantan Choudhury and Nicolas Loizou. [Extragradient Method for $(L_0,L_1)$-Lipschitz Root-finding Problems](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.22421v1). NeurIPS 2025. Complexity: $O(1+R^2(L_0/\varepsilon+L_1)^2)$ exact operator calls for adaptive extragradient to return a queried iterate with $\|F(x)\|\le\varepsilon$.

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Unconstrained operator root finding. The continuous map F from ℝᵈ to ℝᵈ has a root z satisfying the Minty condition ⟨F(x), x−z⟩ ≥ 0 for every x.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: One query at any x returns the full vector F(x) exactly for every query history and oracle seed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x and y, ‖F(x)−F(y)‖ ≤ (L₀+L₁ max_{u∈[x,y]} ‖F(u)‖)‖x−y‖. Continuity ensures the segment maximum exists. The constants L₀ > 0 and L₁ ≥ 0 are public.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries, replies and outputs lie in the full Euclidean space ℝᵈ with public dimension d.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralizedLipschitzMinty.lean, Params.d, spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.Output and spec.publicInput

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The public starting point x₀ and radius R ≥ 0 satisfy ‖x₀−z‖ ≤ R for the same hidden root z that satisfies the Minty condition.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The residual must be integrable and satisfy 𝔼[‖F(X)‖] ≤ ε under the product law of the algorithm and oracle seeds.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The output is one point X in ℝᵈ. Its residual is the Euclidean operator norm ‖F(X)‖ to the first power, with public tolerance ε > 0.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines a Minty inequality about one hidden root with a Lipschitz bound that varies with the operator norm along each segment.
